SURVEY + CHOICE (worker-sable-disperser). Choice: Ben-Sasson & Kopparty, Affine dispersers from subspace polynomials (SICOMP 41(4) 2012; ECCC TR10-044), Theorem 7.3 (Sym^t construction), with one honest adaptation. Rejected: Li O(log n) and Shaltiel (multi-layer extractor machinery, far larger); Bourgain/Yehudayoff/Li11 (exponential sums, only n/sqrt(loglog n)); BK univariate Thm 2.6/2.7 (linear dimension only).
INFEASIBILITY FINDING (prime degree): BK as stated needs block fields F_(2^n) of PRIME degree n ~ 2N^(3/5). Poly-time arithmetic there needs a deterministic poly-time construction of irreducible polynomials of large prime degree (Shoup 1990: deterministic factoring + Kummer towers); brute force is 2^(N^(3/5)). Every elementary explicit family (x^(2*3^k)+x^(3^k)+1, Lidl-Niederreiter Thm 3.35 towers, Kummer towers) has subfields of index 2 or 3, and subfields defeat BK (their Remark 2.4; products over a subfield shift are confined to that shift). So literal BK is out of reach here.
ADAPTATION (feasible): BK's proof of Thm 7.3 uses non-containment in subfield shifts only for blocks with dim Y_i > r+1. Replacing r+1 by M = max(r+1, s), s = largest proper-subfield dimension, the same averaging gives: f is nonconstant on every F2-affine A in F^r with dim A > nr/t + nt + r*M, whenever n*t >= r(r+1). Take n = p_1...p_k, distinct primes in (L, 4L], L ~ 0.3 log2 N, so s <= n/L and r*M <= r(r+1) + N/L. Degree-p_j irreducibles found by brute force (2^O(L) = poly(N)); F = GaloisField 2 n with roots y_j of f_j, bits read in the tensor monomial basis prod_j y_j^(kappa_j) (independent by the coprime-degree tower law); multiplication is polynomial multiplication plus reduction mod each f_j (F2 coefficients). Mathlib Chebyshev.theta_ge / theta_le_log4_mul_x give the primes.
FUNCTION: input x in F2^N. Parameters n (shortest prefix product of primes in (L,4L] with n^9 >= N^5), r = floor(N/n), t = ceil(r(r+1)/n); first n*r bits = r blocks x_i in F; f(x) = Tr( sum over |I|=t of prod_{i in I} x_i^(2^(r+2-i)-1) ). Small N: trivial branch with d(N) = N+1 (vacuous).

With b2's Thm 4.1 this gives 3.5N - O(N/log N): o(N) as the goal asks, honestly weaker than the paper's O(log n).
